text:
maria.ng: Heads-up — found weird rows in the org-sandbox preview where a few prefetch responses include records from other orgs. quick glance looks like a cache key collision when sandbox=true.

sam.k: oof. repro steps?

maria.ng: repro: open sandboxed view -> trigger prefetch endpoint /internal/prefetch?org=123&sandbox=true -> response contains row with org_id=789 in results. happened on prod-canary only.

jen: did you capture request/response headers? any X-Org or Routing tags missing?

maria.ng: yes attached header dump in thread (snip):
```
GET /internal/prefetch?org=123&sandbox=true
headers: {"x-org-id":"123","x-routing-tag":"prefetch-v2","x-feature-sandbox":"true"}
```
response: contains item {"org_id":789,...} and cache-control: hit

sam.k: that smells like cache key normalization issue — sandbox flag not part of cache key. if backend caches by route+org only, sandbox could collide.

jen: or KV cache mutated by prefix reuse. Which service owns the cache? prefetch-service or shared edge-cache?

maria.ng: shared edge-cache (prefetch layer falls back to edge). I think edge cache key is built in edge-proxy.

sam.k: quick mitigation: make edge key include sandbox flag and tenant hash. add header sanitizer to internal-router to refuse cross-org items. could ship a transient blocker rule.

ops-bot: Incident note: suspected multi-tenant exposure, priority P1 if repro on >1 customer. Please escalate if confirmed.

jen: agree on both: short-term guard = server-side validation on prefetch response: assert all returned rows have org_id == request org (or sandbox equivalent). That prevents leakage even if cache wrong. Long-term = fix keying in edge-proxy.

maria.ng: putting together PoC patch for response-assertion now. will open PR.

sam.k: also add telemetry: count of mismatched org rows per response and a per-org metric, emit to console-dashboard so we can alert. link to dashboard: https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/prefetch-leak

jen: add unit + e2e that simulates sandbox+non-sandbox requests hitting the same cache. we should catch this in CI.

maria.ng: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/prefetch-service/pulls/482 — implements response guard + metric + tag in cache key. draft for now.

sam.k: nice. for rollout UX: we should canary the change at edge-proxy and prefetch-service separately. do prefetch-service first with guard only (no key-change) to stop further leakage, then deploy edge-proxy key fix in a follow-up.

jen: agree. plan: 1) merge guard behind feature-flag (sandbox-prefetch-guard) and enable globally. 2) deploy canary to 5% and monitor metric mismatches. 3) if clean, enable 100% and then ship key change.

maria.ng: doing step 1 now. test failing on one legacy integration — looks like some plugins intentionally return cross-tenant refs (old behavior). filing support ticket.

sam.k: we need to evaluate whether that plugin behavior is acceptable; either whitelist or patch plugin to namespace responses.

deploy-bot: canary deployed prefetch-service@hash=abc123 to cluster canary-1 (5%).

ops-bot: Alert rule created: prefetch.mismatch.count > 0 for >5 minutes -> notify #incidents and page oncall.

jen: also add audit log entry whenever guard drops rows. compliance wants audit trail for data-exposure attempts.

maria.ng: added audit event and included sample payload (sanitized) in PR.

sam.k: one more internal API debate: should internal endpoints accept sandbox param or prefer header x-sandbox:true? currently mixed. Recommend normalizing to header only to avoid cache key issues from query string ordering.

jen: +1 header-only. but migrating will require compatibility layer on edge-proxy to translate old clients. schedule for next sprint.

maria.ng: note — the telemetry dashboard already spiked once around 02:14 UTC which matches customer-reported glitch. I'm notifying affected CSMs.

sam.k: thanks. after 100% guard rollout, let's run a small canary of key-change during low traffic window. coordinate with infra for rolling restart.

jen: followups: (1) maria: finish PR + enable feature-flag (2) sam: prepare edge-proxy key-change PR (3) ops: monitor dashboard and escalate if any mismatches.

maria.ng: will update PR with test for the legacy plugin case and add migration note.

sam.k: thx. good catch. :thumbsup:

jen: filing a short postmortem draft and proposed checklist for multi-tenant prefetch to avoid this class in future. will ping for reviewers.

maria.ng: adding contact list for affected accounts in the ticket.

deploy-bot: prefetch-service@abc123 promoted to production (feature-flag enabled) — 100% rollout.
_extra_note: This document is a Slack thread; messages are in chronological order in the 'text' field as a single continuous string.
